megabooks.title: African Plant Medicine
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Traditional plant medicine from across the African continent — West African, East African, South African, and Ethiopian traditions.

components.title: A Catalogue of the Aburi Gardens (1906)
components.contributor: Government Botanical Gardens, Aburi, Gold Coast — colonial record
components.note: A British colonial administration's catalogue of the Gold Coast's botanical garden, recording local plant names and traditional uses as observed and documented by colonial staff. This is an outside observer's record, not a text authored by the West African communities whose knowledge it describes — the closest available primary-source document standing in for a genuinely oral tradition with no single canonical text of its own. 52 real facsimile pages, replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

components.title: The Medicinal and Poisonous Plants of Southern Africa (1932)
components.contributor: John Mitchell Watt & Maria Gerdina Breyer-Brandwijk
components.note: The foundational scientific survey of Southern African medicinal plants, extensively documenting Zulu, Xhosa, Sotho and other traditional usage as recorded by the authors — an outside observer's record rather than a community-authored text, the closest available primary source for a genuinely oral tradition. 350 real facsimile pages, replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

components.title: Useful Plants of Nyasaland
components.contributor: Jessie Williamson, ed. Percy James Greenway — colonial record
components.note: A colonial-era botanical survey of what is now Malawi, documenting local plant uses including traditional medicine — an outside observer's record rather than a community-authored text, the closest available primary source for a genuinely oral tradition. 186 real facsimile pages, replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

components.contributor: Transcribed from the scans by Claude (AI), in English
components.note: A complete AI transcription of an 1906 British colonial catalogue of the Aburi Gardens into readable text, beside the original scans. Unverified.

components.title: Medicinal Plants of Southern Africa — full text (AI transcription)
components.contributor: Transcribed from the scans by Claude (AI), in English
components.note: A complete AI transcription of Watt & Breyer-Brandwijk's 1932 survey of Southern African medicinal plants into readable text, beside the original scans. Unverified.

megabooks.title: Plant Medicine of the Americas
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Indigenous and traditional plant medicine from North America, the Amazon, Mesoamerica, and the Philippines.

components.title: Materia Medica Americana (1787)
components.note: A German physician's field survey of American medicinal plants, based on his 1783-84 travels through the newly independent United States — the earliest systematic scientific study of North American plant medicine. Replaces an earlier synthesized placeholder. 200 real facsimile pages.

components.title: Notes of a Botanist on the Amazon & Andes, Vol. 1 (1908)
components.note: The field notebooks of the great Victorian botanist who spent fifteen years documenting Amazonian plants and their uses among indigenous communities, published posthumously — an outside observer's record rather than a community-authored text, the closest available primary source for a genuinely oral tradition. 350 real facsimile pages (first volume), replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

components.title: Ritual of the Bacabs (Maya medical incantations, c. 1779)
components.contributor: Yucatec Maya healers, copied from an earlier manuscript
components.note: A genuine Maya-language manuscript of medical incantations and herbal remedies — forty-two spells for ailments from seizures to snakebite — replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder. 348 real facsimile pages, Princeton University Library.

components.title: Flora de Filipinas, Vol. 1 (1837)
components.note: A Spanish Augustinian friar's systematic survey of Philippine flora, including medicinal uses documented from local knowledge — replaces an earlier synthesized placeholder. 350 real facsimile pages (first volume).

components.title: The Useful Native Plants of Australia (1889)
components.note: A colonial-era compilation of Australian native plant uses. Maiden himself acknowledged relying on settler and scientific sources rather than direct consultation with Aboriginal communities — an outside observer's record at some remove even from other colonial surveys, offered as the closest available primary-source document standing in for a genuinely oral tradition with no single canonical text of its own. 350 real facsimile pages, replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

megabooks.title: European Botanical Medicine
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Medieval, Celtic, Anglo-Saxon, Italian Renaissance, Russian, Welsh, Norse, and modern European botanical medicine texts — including manuscript facsimiles.

components.title: Bald's Leechbook — Manuscript (c.950 CE)
components.note: England's oldest medical compendium. British Library Royal MS 12 D XVII. 279 pages. A remedy in this book was recently proven to kill MRSA.

components.title: Leechdoms, Wortcunning & Starcraft (1864)
components.note: 546 pages. Cockayne's bilingual edition — Old English original beside English translation. Contains Bald's Leechbook, Old English Herbarium, and the Lacnunga charm collection.

components.title: Erbario — Italian Herbal Manuscript (c.1400)
components.note: 180 botanical illustrations. Human-faced mandrake roots prescribed as anesthetics. The bridge between medieval and Renaissance botanical science.

components.title: Matthioli — Di Pedacio Dioscoride (1544)
components.note: 448 pages. First Italian vernacular translation of Dioscorides. The most influential herbal of the Renaissance. English translation in progress.

components.title: The Physicians of Myddvai (trans. from ancient Welsh mss.)
components.contributor: Rhiwallon and his sons, physicians of Myddfai — trans. John Pughe
components.note: Translated directly from the ancient manuscripts held at Jesus College Oxford, Llanover, and Tonn — replaces an earlier placeholder. 519 real facsimile pages, bilingual Welsh/English.

components.title: De Simplicibus Medicinis Laxativis (ed. Johnsson, 1914)
components.note: A scholarly critical edition of Harpestraeng's medical writings, the direct source tradition behind the surviving Old Norse/Icelandic medical manuscripts (the actual manuscripts, held at Iceland's Arnamagnaean collection, are only accessible through a captcha-gated viewer). 112 real facsimile pages, replacing an earlier synthesized placeholder.

components.title: Russian Travnik — Monastery Herbal Tradition
components.note: Russian Orthodox monastery herbal medicine. Byzantine learning, Central Asian influence, and Siberian plant knowledge — Chaga, Rhodiola, Sea buckthorn.

components.title: German Commission E Monographs
components.contributor: German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices
components.note: 126 evidence-based plant monographs — the gold standard of phytomedicine regulatory review.

components.title: American Herbal Pharmacopoeia
components.note: 45 full-quality plant monographs with clinical evidence review.

components.title: WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants
components.note: 94 validated plant monographs — the authoritative global standard for plant medicine.

megabooks.title: Caribbean Travellers
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: First-person accounts of the Caribbean from the 1820s to the 1890s — captains' logs, colonial administrators' diaries, and naturalists' observations, with extensive firsthand documentation of Anguilla.

components.title: Six Months in the West Indies in 1825
components.note: The richest single account of 1820s Anguilla — a full dedicated chapter.

components.title: Down the Islands: A Voyage to the Caribbees
components.note: Full chapter on Anguilla, Irish settlers, and a 200-year-old French spy's report.

components.title: Gossip of the Caribbees
components.note: Literary account of a colonial administrator's isolated posting to Anguilla — visited monthly by a mail ship.

components.title: Trinidad and the Other West India Islands and Colonies
components.note: Includes dedicated Anguilla section: 1746 French attack repelled, revenue figures, governance.

components.title: The West Indies
components.note: Entire chapter (XX) on Anguilla, St. Martin, Barbuda. Opens with the island's 'snake' name etymology.

megabooks.title: Caribbean History — Primary Documents
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Official documents, legal records, and firsthand historical accounts of the Caribbean from the 1830s to the early 20th century.

components.title: Emancipation in the West Indies
components.contributor: James A. Thome & J. Horace Kimball
components.note: American Quaker delegation's firsthand account of Emancipation Day in Anguilla.

components.title: Les colonies anglaises de 1574 à 1660
components.note: Names Anguilla in Charles I's 1627 Carlisle land grants. Translation ongoing.

components.title: Sailing Directions for the West Indies
components.note: Official nautical directions. Anguilla's coastline, reefs, and the 'Eel' etymology confirmed.

components.title: Modern Geography, Vol. 2

megabooks.title: Caribbean Cartography — 17th to 19th Century
megabooks.author: Various
megabooks.description: Historical nautical charts, Dutch Golden Age maps, and colonial survey maps of the Caribbean — all featuring Anguilla and the Lesser Antilles.

components.title: Pascaerte van de Caribes Eylanden (1675)
components.note: Dutch nautical chart of the Lesser Antilles by a celebrated Dutch ship's pilot.

components.title: Insulae Americanae in Oceano Septentrionali (1634)
components.note: Dutch Golden Age masterpiece. Amsterdam's Blaeu dynasty at its peak.

components.title: A Chart of the Caribe Ilands (1680)
components.note: Official hydrographer to the East India Company and Hudson's Bay Company.

components.title: Isole Antili, la Cuba e la Spagnuola (1690)
components.note: Venetian cosmographer who built globes for Louis XIV.

components.title: Tabula Mexicae et Floridae (1710)
components.note: Amsterdam's Schenk publishing house.

components.title: Carte Réduite des Antilles (1758)
components.note: French hydrographer royal — the authoritative French cartographic view of the Antilles.

components.title: Antillas Menores (1781)
components.note: Spanish royal cartographer's view of the Lesser Antilles.

megabooks.title: The Florentine Codex
megabooks.author: Fray Bernardino de Sahagún
megabooks.description: The most complete surviving account of Aztec civilization at the moment of the Spanish conquest — a bilingual Nahuatl/Spanish encyclopedia compiled by a Franciscan friar working with Nahua scholars and artists over three decades. Twelve books cover the gods, ceremonies, divination, rhetoric, kingship, trade, natural history, and the conquest itself, illustrated throughout by Indigenous tlacuiloque. All twelve volumes, complete, in real facsimile from the Library of Congress copy — 2,439 pages.

components.title: Book 1: The Gods
components.contributor: Fray Bernardino de Sahagún, with Nahua tlacuiloque (scribe-artists)
components.note: 118 real facsimile pages, Library of Congress copy of the Florentine Codex.

components.title: Book 2: The Ceremonies
components.contributor: Fray Bernardino de Sahagún, with Nahua tlacuiloque (scribe-artists)
components.note: 290 real facsimile pages, Library of Congress copy of the Florentine Codex.

components.title: Book 3: The Origin of the Gods
